meta.topic: InkFight stickman animation: keyframes, principles, idles, recoil, cosmetics, mocap

units.time: ticks (sim runs 60 ticks/s, 1 tick = 16.7 ms; film references at 24 fps convert x2.5)
units.angles: radians in body space facing +x, canvas y-down: 0 = forward, -PI/2 = up, PI/2 = down, PI = behind (same as poses.ts abs()); rel() = offset from rest. torso rel(+) leans forward, rel(-) leans back
units.length: px in stickman world units (rest figure is ~180 tall, BODY.h = 170, HEAD_R = 20)

current_state.MOVE_POSES: 2 static poses per move: wind shown for t < mv.from, hit for t <= mv.to + 3, then FIGHT. No in-betweens, so every move pops between 3 poses.
current_state.move_timing: MOVES has dur/from/to; startup (from) ranges 4 (jab) to 16 (axeKick) ticks; active (to - from) 3-8; recovery (dur - to) 7-13
current_state.hitstop: sim.ts: m.freeze = blocked ? 2 : special ? 6 : min(6, 2 + round(dealt/4)); SUPER_FREEZE 16 on special start; KO slow-mo every 3rd tick
current_state.shake: render.ts: random jitter, amplitude special 13 / blocked 2 / normal 4 + dmg/3 / KO 20, decays x0.85 per frame
current_state.smear: render.ts keeps the last 7 tip points from mv.from-2 to mv.to+2 and strokes a trail (width 18, specials 26)
current_state.idle: single sine, period 2*PI*160 ms (~60 ticks), torso +-0.03, head +-0.03, upperF +-0.08; walk = sine period ~40 ticks

shape.why_anchors: at = [anchor, offsetTicks] ties each key to the sim's own phases (start=0, from=mv.from, to=mv.to, end=mv.dur). When balance.ts retunes startup/recovery, the art retimes itself instead of desyncing from the hitbox. Resolve once per move to absolute ticks and clamp to [0, dur], monotonic.
shape.ease_semantics: A key's ease shapes the segment that ENDS at that key (like CSS keyframes). Default 'inOutSine'.
shape.missing_bones: A bone absent from a key inherits the previous key's value (first key inherits FIGHT). Same as the existing spread {...FIGHT, ...}.
shape.interpolation: Resolve abs/rel to local angles with resolvePose for both keys, then lerp each bone on the shortest arc: d = ((b - a + PI) mod 2PI) - PI; v = a + d * ease(u). Exception: spinKick/flip keys may need the long way; mark with flip so the renderer mirrors instead of lerping 2PI.
shape.sub_tick: Evaluate with fractional t = f.t + render alpha so 120/144 Hz monitors stay smooth. During m.freeze f.t does not advance, so the pose freezes automatically (that is the hit-stop impact frame).
shape.lunge: lunge is keyed like a bone (scalar lerp) so body shift peaks with the strike and eases back during recovery, instead of jumping 0 to 12 px.
shape.stretch: optional per-key multiplier on the striking limb's bone length (1.0 = rest), see principles squash_stretch.

easings.name: outQuad
easings.use: into the anticipation pose: fast start, slows into the coil so the eye reads the wind-up

easings.name: inOutSine
easings.use: moving hold / coil drift (last ticks of startup), idle loops

easings.name: inExpo
easings.use: the strike segment (anticipation to overshoot): almost no motion then all of it in the last tick; with 1-3 tick strike segments this reads as a snap

easings.name: snap
easings.use: strike segments of 1 tick: jump straight to the target (step). Fighting games commonly use 1-2 drawings between anticipation and contact and fill the gap with a smear

easings.name: outBack
easings.use: settle from overshoot back to the hit pose, landing squash recovery, getup end, idle re-entry

easings.name: outCubic
easings.use: follow-through after active frames: the limb keeps going and decelerates

easings.name: inOutCubic
easings.use: recovery back to FIGHT: slow out of the extended pose, slow into guard (slow-in/slow-out)

easings.name: outExpo
easings.use: hit reactions: victim snaps to recoil within 1-2 ticks, then drifts

auto_convert_wind_hit.summary: Generate 6 keys from each existing {wind, hit, lunge} so no move needs hand re-authoring; hand-tune only the showcase moves later.
auto_convert_wind_hit.helpers: extrap(a, b, k) = per-bone a + (b - a) * k on resolved local angles (k > 1 overshoots past b). FIGHT is the neutral pose.

keys.note: current pose; in practice blend from whatever pose the fighter was in (chain/cancel)
anticipation reached at 60% of startup (jab from=4: tick 2)
coil: moving hold 8% deeper, body draws back slightly. Skip when from <= 4 (no room)

keys.ease: snap if from-1 to from+1 is 2 ticks else inExpo
keys.note: overshoot / impact frame, aligned with first active tick

keys.pose: hit with distal bones (fore*, shin*, head) pushed +0.15 rad further along hit-wind direction
keys.note: follow-through; proximal bones settle to hit, distal ones keep travelling
recovery; blend idle loop weight 0 to 1 over the last 40% so there is no pop into idle

auto_convert_wind_hit.spin_moves: keep spin: flip = true on keys from the coil until to+2; renderer mirrors instead of lerping.
auto_convert_wind_hit.specials: specialPose already branches on t thresholds (t < 10 etc). Convert each branch boundary to a key at the same tick with ease inExpo for the release and outBack for holds; leave looping parts (beam wobble, spiral run, barrage) procedural.
auto_convert_wind_hit.check: assert every move's resolved keys are strictly increasing and the overshoot key lands inside [from, to]; scripts/check-stats.ts style self-check.

principles.rule: Anticipation (reaching the wind pose) takes ~60% of startup; the last 1-2 startup ticks are the strike. Never less than 1 tick of anticipation: even one frame makes a move readable. For our moves: jab (from 4) = 2 ticks wind + 2 strike; cross (6) = 4 + 2; roundhouse (11) = 7 wind incl. 2 coil + 2 strike; axeKick (16) = 10 + 2-3 coil + 2.
principles.source: S1 (Cartwright, Skullgirls GDC 2014: 'even a frame of anticipation'), S2 (anticipation is a design/animation trade-off in games)

principles.rule: Wind-up moves opposite to the strike: torso rel -0.1 to -0.3 for punches, striking limb drawn back 0.3-0.6 rad past guard, body lunge -0.15x before +lunge. The bigger the move's mult, the bigger the counter-motion (scale wind offset by mult: jab 0.7x, spinKick 1.9x).
principles.source: S2, S5 (Illusion of Life principles via Game Developer)

principles.rule: On the first active tick the striking chain goes 8-15% past the hit pose (stretch limb length x1.10-1.15), holds through hit-stop, then settles back to the hit pose in 3-4 ticks with outBack. One overshoot frame is enough.
principles.source: S1 (one frame overshooting the target then pulling back adds power)

principles.rule: After active ends, distal bones (forearm, shin, head, held item) lag their parents by 2 ticks and travel 0.15-0.3 rad further before returning. Heavy items (mace, big sword) lag 3-4 ticks and 0.3-0.45 rad. Use follow-through to fill gaps when there are no in-betweens.

Recovery returns to FIGHT with inOutCubic over (dur - to) ticks; the final 15-20% uses a small outBack (1.03-1.05 overshoot into guard) so the fighter 'lands' in stance. Fade idle-loop weight in over the last 40% of recovery.
principles.source: S2 (slow-in/slow-out), S9 (Rosen: blend procedural layers over few keys)

principles.rule: No pose is fully static for more than ~6 ticks (except intentional hit-stop). During holds (beam hold, block, charge) keep 30% of the archetype idle amplitude running plus 1-2% drift toward the next key.

Draw a smear only on ticks where the striking tip moves more than ~20 px/tick (about one head radius), typically the 1-2 strike ticks and the first active tick. Life 2-4 ticks, alpha 0.9 -> 0. Draw it as a tapered filled polygon (width = 3x pen width at the tip, 0 at the tail) along the arc from the anticipation tip position to the overshoot position, so it shows start, motion and end. Keep it visible (frozen) during hit-stop. For spins use 2-3 ghost limbs at 35%/20% alpha (multiples) instead of a ribbon.
principles.source: S1 (smear shows start, motion, end), S8 (smear = stylized motion blur; Overwatch uses them for fast motion and weight)

principles.rule: Freeze both fighters on contact, scaled by hit weight. Suggested: blocked 3, light (jab, low kick) 5-6, medium (cross, hook, front kick) 7-9, heavy (roundhouse, spinKick, axeKick, uppercut) 10-13, special connect 14-16, KO hit 18-20 then slow-mo. Formula: freeze = clamp(round(4 + dealt * 0.35), 4, 13), special 15. Our current cap of 6 is short of genre norms (SF2 ~10 frames; Smash Ultimate floor(d*0.65 + 6), cap 30). Note: freeze changes sim timing (authoritative host), so tune with scripts/balance.ts.
principles.source: S3 (critpoints: SF2 ~10 frames hitstop, hitstop helps the eye register impact), S4 (SSBWiki hitlag formulas and caps), S6 (Sakurai on hitstop)

principles.rule: During hit-stop the attacker holds still; the victim vibrates along the hit direction: offset alternates sign every tick, amplitude 3 px light / 5 px heavy, decaying linearly to 0 over the freeze. Ground hits shake horizontally, air hits vertically.
principles.source: S3, S4 (Smash characters vibrate during hitlag: horizontal on ground, vertical in air)

principles.rule: Replace per-frame Math.random jitter with a trauma model: trauma += hit amount (cap 1), decays 0.03/tick; offset = maxShake * trauma^2 * noise(t), noise = sum of 2 sines with incommensurate frequencies (e.g. 0.9 and 1.37 rad/tick) per axis. maxShake = 16 px, optional rotation 0.015 rad. Trauma: blocked 0.15, light 0.25 (1 px), medium 0.4 (2.6 px), heavy 0.55 (4.8 px), special 0.75 (9 px), KO 1.0 (16 px). Add a 1-tick directional kick of 2-4 px along the hit direction first. Squaring makes small hits subtle and big hits strong.
principles.source: S7 (Eiserloh GDC 2016 trauma^2 + noise shake), S10 (Nijman 'Art of Screenshake': camera kick back plus quickly decaying shake)

principles.rule: Bones are fixed length, so fake volume with bone-length and stroke-width scale: striking limb length x1.10-1.15 and stroke width x0.85 on the overshoot tick; jump take-off whole-body scaleY 1.08 / scaleX 0.95 for 2-3 ticks; landing scaleY 0.88 / scaleX 1.10 for 3-4 ticks then outBack to 1; victim torso length x0.92 for 1 tick on a body hit. Scale about the feet (y = 0) so the floor contact holds. Keep scaleX * scaleY ~ 1.
principles.source: S2, S5 (squash and stretch, volume preservation)

principles.rule: On the first hit-stop tick of heavy/special hits draw one inverted or ink-flood frame (or 1-2 tick white flash at alpha 0.6-0.8) and the impact ring at max size; resume normal render on tick 2. Never more than 2 ticks (photosensitivity), and not for light hits.
principles.source: S1, S3 (hitsparks/impact feedback show contact point)

principles.rule: Few strong keys plus procedural layers beat many keys: 4-6 keys per normal move, 6-10 per special, procedural idle/breath/secondary motion on top. Overgrowth reportedly animated whole characters from a handful of keys plus physics/procedural blending.
principles.source: S9 (Rosen GDC 2014 'An Indie Approach to Procedural Animation')

principles.rule: The overshoot key must read in silhouette: striking limb near full extension (angle between upper and fore < 0.25 rad for straights), torso rotated toward the target, back arm pulled to the chest. Check by rendering keys as black silhouettes at 50% size.

idle_loops.method: Each bone value = base + A * sin(2PI * (t/period + phase)) + 0.3 * A * sin(2PI * (t/(period*1.618) + phase2)). The second, non-integer-period sine stops the loop looking mechanical. Phase is a fraction of the cycle; a positive phase lag on child bones = overlapping action. Body bob is done by bending thighs/shins (the renderer keeps the lowest foot on the floor), float is a root y offset that needs a new BodyMotion field (e.g. lift: px). Randomize the global phase per fighter so two idles never sync.

archetypes.extra: shoulder pads rise 1 px on inhale; no foot shuffle; every 6-9 s a 30-tick 'shoulder roll' accent (upper* +0.15 rad)

archetypes.feel: on the toes, rhythmic boxer bounce

bones.note: opposite to thigh = knee flex, ~4 px bob

archetypes.extra: weight shift: lunge +-2 px at period 72 (every 2nd bounce); lead fist pumps (foreF +0.2) every ~3 s

archetypes.feel: weightless hover, limbs drifting like underwater

bones.note: base lift 6-10 px off floor with a soft ink shadow ellipse that shrinks as lift grows

archetypes.extra: distal amplitude > proximal and growing lag = drag; orbs orbit at period 90 (see cosmetics)

archetypes.feel: composed, blade tip barely moving, calm breathing
archetypes.extra: slow weight shift lunge +-1.5 px at period 180; every 4-6 s a 20-tick grip adjust (foreF -0.12 then back, outBack)

archetypes.feel: wide low crouch, weapon hanging like a pendulum

bones.note: thighF abs(DOWN-0.6), thighB abs(DOWN+0.6), torso rel(0.12) forward lean
mace arm swings as pendulum, lagging the body

archetypes.extra: item angle lags foreF by 4 ticks (spring k 0.15, damping 0.8) so the mace head swings after the arm

recoil.timing: Snap into the recoil pose in 1-2 ticks (outExpo), hold through hit-stop (with victim shake), drift 10% further during hitstun, recover to FIGHT with outBack over the last 30% of hitstun. Pick the variant from the hit height (sim already has top/bot per move) and scale offsets by min(1.5, 0.6 + knock/10).

head_hit.when: contact above the shoulder line (high hits, uppercuts, headbutt, roundhouse/axe to head)
head_hit.note: head snaps back first, torso follows 1 tick later (overlap); arms fling forward relative to the body. Uppercut variant: head rel(-0.9), torso rel(-0.5), small lift 6-10 px.

body_hit.when: contact between shoulder and hip (crosses, palms, knees, front kicks)
body_hit.note: folds over the gut, hips pushed back, arms clutch the stomach; torso length x0.92 for 1 tick (squash)

low_hit.note: front leg knocked back, arms out for balance

blocked.pose: block pose plus torso rel(-0.08), head rel(-0.1), forearms pushed back 0.15
blocked.note: 1-tick snap, 3-tick return; blue spark already drawn

knockdown.launch: torso rel(-0.7), head rel(-0.5), limbs trail (upper* rel(+-1.0)); whole-body fall angle rises toward -1.45 like the KO topple, root follows the sim's arc
knockdown.fall: fall angle 0 to -1.45 over 14-20 ticks with inQuad (gravity look)
knockdown.ground_contact: 1 tick squash (scaleY 0.85), bounce 6-10 px up over 6 ticks, second contact without bounce; limbs flop with 1-2 tick lag (or a cheap verlet on hands/feet); dust/ink splat

getup.pose: roll to side, fall -0.9, thighF abs(DOWN-1.2), shinF abs(DOWN+0.8), handB on floor
kneeling: fall 0, thighF abs(-0.2), shinF abs(DOWN), thighB abs(DOWN+0.3), shinB abs(BACK-0.2), torso rel(0.3)

knockdown.gameplay_note: getup length and invulnerability are sim rules (not cosmetic); 24-30 ticks matches the animation above.

recoil.ko: existing topple is good; add a 1-tick ground squash, a 4 px bounce, the head drawing rolling 0.3 rad, and the held item dropping with a simple gravity + spin arc (it detaches at contact).

cosmetics.general: All are render-only (never in the sim, never synced), drawn in the fighter's ink colour with the drawing's pen width, so they look hand-drawn. Seed per-fighter jitter from the character id so strokes do not boil every frame; optionally re-seed every 6-8 ticks for a deliberate 'line boil' look. Verlet state lives in the Renderer per slot; reset it on teleport, round start and facing flip (mirror stored points across the hip x).

items.approach: Anchor at hip joint, angle = torso world angle + 2.4 rad (pointing back-down), length = 0.7 x sword length. ctx.save; translate(hip); rotate(angle); draw a rounded rect (roundRect, w 8 px) filled with paper colour then stroked in ink; 2 short cross strokes for the throat. Draw before the back leg so it sits behind. Optional: angle follows torso through a 1-float spring (k 0.2, damping 0.75) for a small swing on lunges.

items.for: Fighter / boxing, Muay Thai, street styles
items.approach: On foreF/foreB, over the last 25% of the bone: 3-4 short strokes perpendicular to the bone (length = 1.6 x pen width), each rotated a seeded +-0.15 rad and spaced 4 px, plus one loop around the fist (arc r = pen width * 1.4). White or accent fill under ink outline. Trailing tape tail (2-point verlet, 6 px) optional.
items.cost: about 8 lines per fighter per frame

items.approach: N = 2-3 orbs around the head or back hand: pos = anchor + (cos(w t + phi_i) * rx, sin(w t + phi_i) * ry), rx 34 px, ry = 0.35 rx (pseudo-3D ellipse), w = 2PI/90 per tick, phi_i = i * 2PI/N. depth z = sin(w t + phi_i): draw orbs with z < 0 before the body and z >= 0 after; radius x (0.85 + 0.15 z). Trail: keep last 6 positions, stroke a tapered line. Glow: drawImage a pre-rendered radial-gradient sprite (offscreen canvas, made once per colour), never shadowBlur per frame. On special charge, shrink rx and speed w x3 so orbs spiral into the hand.
items.cost: 3 drawImage + 3 short paths; shadowBlur avoided (it is the expensive part)

items.approach: Verlet chain of 5 points (4 segments, L = 11 px). p0 pinned each tick to the shoulder joint offset 6 px behind (facing-aware). Integrate per tick at fixed 60 Hz: next = p + (p - prev) * 0.92 + (0, 0.35) gravity + wind, where wind = -facing * |body vx| * 0.4 plus sin noise 0.1. Then 3 constraint passes: move each pair to distance L (half each, p0 fixed). Body collision: in body-local space clamp points to stay behind the spine line (x <= shoulder.x + 2). Draw a ribbon: offset each point perpendicular by half-width growing 6 to 10 px root to tip, fill with accent at 0.85 alpha, stroke the outline with quadraticCurveTo through midpoints. On hit-stop, skip integration (cape freezes too).
items.cost: 5 points x 3 passes per tick, one filled path; well under 0.05 ms

items.approach: Half-dome at the shoulder joint: ellipse rx 14, ry 9 px, rotation = 0.5 * (torso world angle + PI/2) + 0.5 * upper arm world angle so it follows the arm partly. Back pad drawn before the back arm, front pad after the front arm. Fill paper, stroke ink, 2-3 seeded hatch strokes for shading. Lift 1 px with the idle inhale.

Band: two parallel arcs across the head circle at 40% from the top, rotated with the head bone, clipped to the head circle (ctx.clip on an arc) so it wraps the drawn head. Knot at the back: 2 tails, each a 3-point verlet (L 9 px, gravity 0.15, damping 0.9) pinned at the knot; add sin flutter (amp 2 px, period 20 ticks) scaled by body speed when walking/dashing.

cosmetics.verlet_reference: Position-based Verlet with iterative distance constraints (Jakobsen, Hitman: Codename 47) is stable at fixed timesteps and needs no velocities; 2-4 passes are enough for short chains.

bvh_to_2d.summary: Offline script (e.g. scripts/bvh-to-keys.ts), outputs TS key constants; ship no raw mocap files.
steps: Parse HIERARCHY (joint OFFSETs, CHANNELS with per-joint rotation order such as 'Zrotation Xrotation Yrotation') and MOTION (Frames, Frame Time; CMU is 120 fps, resample to 60 by taking every 2nd frame or interpolating).

3D forward kinematics per frame: local R = product of axis rotations in the listed channel order (degrees to radians); global_j = global_parent * Translate(offset_j) * R_j; root also applies its Xposition/Yposition/Zposition channels. Collect world joint positions.

Pick the side-view plane: up = world Y (BVH convention). Facing per clip: fwd = normalize(cross(up, rightHip - leftHip)) averaged over the clip (or flip sign so the strike moves +fwd). Project: x2 = dot(p - hips, fwd), y2 = -dot(p - hips, up) (canvas y-down).

Map joints: hip = Hips; shoulder = midpoint of L/R shoulder (or Spine top/Neck); head = Head (end site); F limbs = lead side (the hand/foot with the larger mean x2 over the active frames, i.e. the striking or nearer-to-opponent side), B = the other.

Angles: for limb bones emit abs(atan2(child.y - parent.y, child.x - parent.x)), which already matches poses.ts (0 forward, -PI/2 up). torso = atan2(shoulder - hip) emitted as rel(angle + PI/2). head = rel((shoulder->head angle) - (torso angle)) relative to its rest.
Foreshortening guard: if a bone's projected length < 30% of its 3D length, its 2D angle is unstable; hold the previous frame's angle or blend toward it by (1 - ratio/0.3).
Unwrap each angle curve (add +-2PI so consecutive frames differ by < PI) before reduction.

Key reduction: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker on all bone curves jointly (tolerance ~0.05 rad) or keep extremes (velocity zero crossings) plus contact frame; fit each segment's ease by least error against the easing set above.
Retime: map the clip's contact frame to MOVES[name].from, its end of follow-through to .to + 2 and the return to stance to .dur, i.e. emit at = [anchor, offset] keys so the sim stays authoritative.
Mirroring is free: the renderer already flips by facing. Validate by rendering the keys next to the projected mocap skeleton.
